reading.general_standard: Can show understanding of main ideas of stories when they are heard and supported with pictures.

speaking.general_standard: Can identify things using simple words during simple exchanges.

specific_standards.receptive: Follow very simple classroom instructions with visual cues.

Can respond to simple questions with sound effects or gestures (e.g., 'What sound is this?').
Can respond to simple classroom commands during listening activities (e.g., 'Sit down').

reading.general_standard: Can show understanding of main ideas of stories when they are heard and supported with pictures.

specific_standards.reading_2: Match spoken words to their written form as they are heard and supported with pictures.

Can match spoken words to their written form when supported by pictures (e.g., matching flashcards with pictures of domestic animals, such as a 'rooster,' to the corresponding written word).
Can identify letters at the beginning of familiar animal names (e.g., C for 'cat').

speaking.general_standard: Can identify things using simple words during simple exchanges.

specific_standards.productive: Identify things in simple pictures, using isolated words.

Can respond to 'What sound?' questions by mimicking the animal sound (e.g., the teacher says, 'What does the cat say?' and the student says, 'Meow!').

writing.general_standard: Can communicate simple ideas by copying words and using drawings and symbols.

listening.general_standard: Can recognize familiar spoken sounds, words and phrases with the support of gestures, simple words and phrases.

specific_standards.receptive: Show comprehension of basic commands used in the classroom.

learning_outcomes: Can show comprehension of simple movement instructions during songs (e.g., 'jump' or 'clap').
Can repeat simple rhymes and songs in group activities that involve listening for action words (e.g., jumps when the song says 'jump').
Can respond to oral instructions for basic dance movements (e.g., 'step forward, step back').

reading.general_standard: Can show understanding of main ideas of stories when they are heard and supported with pictures.

specific_standards.reading_1: Show comprehension of storybook sequencing by pointing to pictures with the teacher's guidance.
specific_standards.reading_2: Match spoken words to their written form as they are heard and supported with pictures.

learning_outcomes: Can show comprehension of storybook sequencing by pointing to pictures with teacher guidance (e.g., pointing to pictures of a character walking, then jumping, and finally dancing in a story).
Can match spoken action words to their written form when supported by pictures (e.g., matching the spoken word 'dance' to a picture of a person dancing and the word 'dance').
Can recognize letters of the alphabet in familiar words (e.g., 'J' in 'jump').

speaking.general_standard: Can identify things using simple words during simple exchanges.

specific_standards.interactive: Engage with simple commands using basic words and gestures.

learning_outcomes: Can recite simple action rhymes (e.g., 'head, shoulders, knees, and toes').
Can give very simple commands to peers (e.g., says 'head,' point to head).
Can participate in conversations about movements, giving simple commands (e.g., 'shake' or 'turn').

writing.general_standard: Can communicate simple ideas by copying words and using drawings and symbols.
learning_outcomes: Can draw and label simple movements in pictures (e.g., drawing a person jumping and writing 'jump').
Can engage in interactive labeling activities by matching labels to pictures of simple movements (e.g., 'run' for a picture of running).
Can trace letters and simple movement-related words (e.g., 'hop' or 'run').

mediation.general_standard: Can use basic strategies to support understanding, such as clarification and repetition.

specific_standards.concept: Use gestures and drawings to link daily routines to classroom activities that are performed.

learning_outcomes: Can use gestures and drawings to express movement actions (e.g., jumping up and down).
Can clarify or ask for repetition when unsure about movement instructions (e.g., 'Repeat, please.').
Can act out scenes from picture books or songs involving dance movements (e.g., making a dance movement seen in the video of a song).

recommended_grammatical_features: Sequential commands with numbers (e.g., 'First, take one step to the side.' 'Next, take two steps to the side.')
Simple directive phrases (e.g., 'Move to the front.' 'Step to the side.')
Positional commands with prepositions (e.g., 'Stand next to the chair.' 'Jump over the line.')

pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.phonemic_awareness: Recognizing letters of the alphabet in familiar words (e.g., 'J' in 'jump') and introducing letters and sounds (S, T, U, V)

pragmatic_competences: Acting out dance commands: Follow simple movement instructions in dance, like 'step forward' and 'clap'
Reciting action rhymes: Participate in action rhymes or songs, such as 'Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Toes'
communicative_competences.sociolinguistic_competences: Group participation: Engaging in group movements and dances, using polite expressions such as 'after you' and 'go ahead'.

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Dance Sequence Video

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Dance & Count Activity
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students will practice counting and dance movements together (e.g., 'Take three steps forward.').

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Digital Dance Video

assessment_ideas.technology_integration: Use a tablet to record the dance routine and play it back to the class for review.

listening.general_standard: Can recognize familiar spoken sounds, words and phrases with the support of gestures, simple words and phrases.
learning_outcomes: Can recognize and respond to words related to emotions (e.g., 'happy,' 'sad,' or 'excited').
Can follow instructions to express feelings, using gestures or facial expressions (e.g., Smiling in response to the prompt 'Show happiness.').
Can participate in activities to identify or describe emotions when spoken (e.g., identifying emotions by pointing to the flashcard that represents the emotion when it is heard).

reading.general_standard: Can show understanding of main ideas of stories when they are heard and supported with pictures.

specific_standards.reading_1: Match spoken words to their written form as they are heard and supported with pictures.
specific_standards.reading_2: Participate in choral reading sessions, supported by the teacher.

learning_outcomes: Can match pictures of facial expressions (e.g., smiling, frowning) to words like 'happy' or 'sad'.

Can recognize simple emotion-related words in choral reading with support from the teacher (e.g., clapping when hearing the word 'happy' and pointing to a picture of a sad face when hearing the word 'sad' during choral reading).
Can recognize letters of the alphabet in familiar words related to feelings and emotions (e.g., pointing to the letter 'H' in the word 'happy' and saying 'H').

speaking.general_standard: Can identify things using simple words during simple exchanges.

specific_standards.productive: Use simple words to express basic needs.
specific_standards.interactive: Express likes or dislikes using simple words and pointing.

learning_outcomes: Can express likes or dislikes about feelings and preferences using simple phrases and gestures (e.g., pointing and saying, 'I like being calm.' 'I don't like feeling tired.').
Can respond to questions about feelings and needs with simple 'I'm...' statements (e.g., 'How are you?' 'I'm excited.' 'I'm tired.').
Can use 'I'm...' phrases along with gestures to express emotions and basic needs (e.g., saying 'I'm hot.' while fanning themselves or 'I'm sad.' with a frown).

writing.general_standard: Can communicate simple ideas by copying words and using drawings and symbols.

specific_standards.productive: Practice tracing and copying letters of the alphabet.

learning_outcomes: Can trace letters and words that describe emotions, with teacher guidance (e.g., 'sad' or 'happy').
Can engage in interactive labeling activities by matching words to pictures of emotions (e.g., labeling 'happy' under a smiling face).
Can draw and label facial expressions (e.g., 'sad' or 'angry').

mediation.general_standard: Can use basic strategies to support understanding, such as clarification and repetition.

specific_standards.communication: Relay messages from teacher to peers.

learning_outcomes: Can use gestures to relay the meaning of emotion-related language to peers (e.g., smiling to show 'I'm happy.').
Can use gestures and miming to relay information about basic needs (e.g., rubbing the stomach to show 'I'm hungry.').
Can interpret and convey simple 'I'm...' statements using body language (e.g., pretending to sleep to indicate 'I'm tired.').

pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.phonemic_awareness: Recognizing letters of the alphabet in familiar words (e.g., 'E' in the word 'rest' or 'H' in the word 'happy') and introducing letters and sounds (W, X, Y, Z)

pragmatic_competences: Expressing feelings and needs: Express emotions and needs by saying, 'I'm happy.' or 'I'm tired.'
Responding to questions about feelings: Answering 'How are you?' with simple 'I'm...' statements (e.g., 'I'm excited.')
communicative_competences.sociolinguistic_competences: Discussing feelings: Talking about emotions and recognizing others' feelings.

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Emotion Faces Chart

twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Create a bingo game with different feelings (e.g., 'happy' or 'tired') and play a matching game based on classmates' feelings.

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Digital Emotion Wheel
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Use a digital tool to create an emotion wheel, labeling different feelings and practicing words like 'I'm excited!'.

skills: Emotional Awareness: Identifying and expressing emotions.
assessment_ideas.technology_integration: Use a drawing app or tablet to create and color the emotion faces or wheel.

specific_standards.receptive: Show comprehension of basic commands used in the classroom.
specific_standards.interactive: Engage in basic interactive games with instructions.

learning_outcomes: Can show comprehension of words related to school activities by responding with gestures, actions, or simple words in listening games like 'Bingo' (e.g., 'Show me what you like: games or puzzles?', and the students point to or say puzzles or games).
Can engage with instructions during interactive games (e.g., 'Point to your book.').
Can respond to simple oral prompts with one or two words related to school activities (e.g., 'Do you like games or math?' 'I like games.' 'I like math.').

reading.general_standard: Can show understanding of main ideas of stories when they are heard and supported with pictures.

specific_standards.reading_1: Participate in choral reading sessions, supported by the teacher.
specific_standards.reading_2: Recognize basic familiar words supported with illustrations or visual aids.

learning_outcomes: Can recognize basic familiar words related to personal preferences (e.g., 'math' or 'like') when supported with illustrations or visual aids (e.g., recognizing the word 'math' while looking at a picture of numbers).

Can participate in choral reading by recognizing and producing the beginning sounds of familiar words related to personal preferences, such as 'science,' 'music,' or 'art' (e.g., identifying and producing the /s/ sound for the letter 'S' in 'science' during group reading).

Can recognize familiar letters in words related to personal preferences, such as 'math' and 'like' (e.g., recognizing the letter 'M' in 'math' and the letter 'L' in 'like' when supported with pictures).

speaking.general_standard: Can identify things using simple words during simple exchanges.

specific_standards.productive: Identify things in simple pictures, using isolated words.
specific_standards.interactive: Express likes or dislikes using simple words and pointing.

learning_outcomes: Can identify things in simple pictures, using isolated words (e.g., 'art' or 'games').
Can express likes or dislikes to peers using simple words and pointing (e.g., 'I like music!' while pointing to a picture).
Can respond to simple questions like 'Do you like it?' with 'yes' or 'no' and gestures (e.g., nodding).

writing.general_standard: Can communicate simple ideas by copying words and using drawings and symbols.

specific_standards.productive: Write simple words with model guidance.

learning_outcomes: Can write simple words related to school preferences with model guidance (e.g., writing 'games' or 'math' by copying from a model or example).
Can copy and trace letters related to school activities (e.g., tracing 'P' for 'painting,' 'A' for 'Art').
Can draw and label favorite school activities collaboratively (e.g., drawing a math book and labeling it 'math').

mediation.general_standard: Can use basic strategies to support understanding, such as clarification and repetition.

specific_standards.text: Identify objects on the pages of picture books, using simple words.

learning_outcomes: Can identify familiar objects in picture books by saying simple words to a peer (e.g., 'game' or 'pencil') when asked or when another student shows interest.
Can use gestures or point to objects in picture books to help peers understand preferences (e.g., pointing to a book and saying 'book' to support a peer's understanding).
Can help a peer understand preferences by connecting words to objects in picture books (e.g., saying 'I like books.' while pointing to a book or 'This is math.' when pointing to numbers).

pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness.phonemic_awareness: Recognizing sounds of letters of the alphabet in the words 'math' and 'games'

pragmatic_competences: Expressing likes and dislikes: Use simple phrases like 'I like...' or 'I don't like...' to express preferences
Answering preference questions: Respond to 'Do you like it?' with 'yes' or 'no'
communicative_competences.sociolinguistic_competences: Sharing preferences: Discussing what students like or dislike about school and activities.

twenty_first_century_projects.title: My Favorite Things Collage
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Students will use words and pictures to create a collage of things they like about school (e.g., 'I like games.' 'I like math.').

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Likes & Dislikes Chart
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Create a chart with columns for 'likes' and 'dislikes' and have students add items they like or dislike (e.g., 'I like books.' 'I don't like books.').

twenty_first_century_projects.title: Digital Favorite Things Poster
twenty_first_century_projects.overview: Take pictures and use a presentation tool to make a digital collage.

skills: Creativity: Designing a collage or poster.
assessment_ideas.technology_integration: Use a simple photo-editing or collage-making app to create a digital version of the project.
